why: A flare-up is a temporary increase in symptoms. A prepared, flexible response can reduce panic and help you return to your plan.

slides.title: A Flare-Up Is Not a Reset
slides.content: A difficult day does not erase the capacity, knowledge, or confidence you have already built.

slides.title: First, Check the Situation
slides.content: Consider whether this resembles a familiar fluctuation or follows a new injury or concerning change. Seek appropriate care when the presentation is new or unsafe.

slides.title: Reduce the Alarm
slides.content: Use the strategies that are safe and familiar to you: slower breathing, a comfortable position, gentle movement, heat or cold when appropriate, and support from someone you trust.

slides.title: Adjust—Do Not Abandon
slides.content: You may temporarily modify the dose, duration, range, or intensity. Complete rest is not automatically required, and pushing through is not always useful either.

slides.title: Return Gradually
slides.content: As the flare settles, work back toward your usual routine. Review what may have contributed without blaming yourself.
